Hair Loss Issues

Understand what your hair
is trying to tell you.

Different patterns of hair loss need different treatment plans.
Start by identifying what you are experiencing.

Hair Loss

Changes in hair density, growth or shedding.

Male Pattern Baldness

Gradual thinning at the temples, crown or hairline.

Female Pattern Hair Loss

Thinning across the scalp, wider parting or reduced volume.

Receding Hairline

Hairline moving back at the temples or forehead.

Thinning Hair

Reduced density or weaker strands that leave hair looking finer.

Crown Hair Loss

Visible thinning or balding at the crown.

Excessive Hair Shedding

More hair falling out than usual each day.

View more

Hair loss can show up in everyday ways. From how you style it to how you feel in photos, small changes can become increasingly noticeable over time.

Frequently Asked Questions

Hair Loss & Diagnosis

Understand common hair-loss concerns and what to expect from a clinical assessment.

Why am I losing my hair?

Hair loss can have many causes, including genetics, hormonal changes, stress, nutritional factors, scalp conditions, certain medications and ageing. The first step is understanding the pattern and possible cause before deciding on treatment.

How do I know what type of hair loss I have?

Hair loss can appear differently from person to person — from a receding hairline and crown thinning to diffuse thinning or increased shedding. A clinical assessment helps identify the pattern, scalp condition and other factors that may be contributing.

Should I wait until my hair loss gets worse before seeking treatment?

Not necessarily. Some forms of hair loss are easier to manage when addressed earlier. An assessment can help determine whether you need treatment now, monitoring, or simply reassurance.

Is hair loss different for men and women?

Yes. Men commonly experience patterned recession around the hairline, temples and crown, while women may experience wider parting or more diffuse thinning. However, every case is different and should be assessed individually.

Treatments & Options

Explore surgical and non-surgical options, and how a treatment plan is chosen.

What treatments are available for hair loss?

Treatment depends on the cause and stage of hair loss. Options may include medical hair-loss treatment, PRP therapy, scalp treatments, laser therapy, hair transplantation and other supportive treatments.

Do I need a hair transplant?

Not everyone does. Some patients may benefit from non-surgical treatment, especially when hair loss is still developing or existing follicles can potentially be preserved. Hair transplantation is generally considered when restoring areas where significant permanent hair loss has already occurred.

Can hair loss be treated without surgery?

Yes. Depending on the condition, non-surgical approaches may help reduce further loss, improve scalp health or support existing hair. Your treatment plan should depend on the diagnosis rather than starting with a specific procedure.

Can different treatments be combined?

In some cases, yes. Hair restoration may involve more than one approach — for example, managing existing hair while restoring areas that have already lost significant density. The combination depends on your condition and treatment goals.

Hair Transplant

Learn about the procedure, suitability, graft planning and comfort during treatment.

How does a hair transplant work?

A hair transplant relocates healthy hair follicles from a donor area — usually at the back or sides of the scalp — into areas affected by permanent hair loss. The placement and direction of the grafts are planned to create a natural-looking result.

Am I suitable for a hair transplant?

Suitability depends on several factors including your hair-loss pattern, donor hair availability, scalp condition, medical history and expectations. A consultation is needed before confirming whether transplantation is appropriate.

How many grafts will I need?

There is no standard number. The graft requirement depends on the size of the area being restored, existing density, donor availability, hair characteristics and the result you are trying to achieve.

Is a hair transplant painful?

Hair transplantation is normally performed under local anaesthesia. Patients may feel some pressure or temporary discomfort during certain stages, but the treatment area is numbed during the procedure.

Results & Expectations

Find answers about hair growth, natural-looking results and long-term expectations.

When will I see results after a hair transplant?

Hair transplant results develop gradually rather than immediately. The transplanted hair goes through several stages of healing, shedding and new growth before the final appearance develops over the following months.

Will my transplanted hair look natural?

Natural-looking results depend heavily on planning — particularly the hairline design, graft distribution, angle, direction and how the new hair integrates with your existing hair.

Will my hair continue to thin after a transplant?

A transplant restores hair in selected areas, but existing non-transplanted hair may continue to change over time. This is why long-term planning and management of existing hair can be important.

Can you guarantee a specific density or result?

Hair restoration is a medical procedure and results vary between individuals. Factors such as donor density, hair characteristics, healing, the extent of hair loss and future progression all influence the final result.

Recovery & Aftercare

Know what to expect after your procedure, from scalp care to returning to daily activities.

How long does recovery take?

Many patients are able to return to light daily activities within a few days. Small scabs, redness or mild swelling may be visible during the early healing period and gradually settle.

When can I return to work?

This depends on the type of work you do and how comfortable you are with the appearance of the scalp during the early recovery period. Many patients plan several days away from work before returning.

When can I exercise again?

Strenuous exercise is usually avoided during the early healing period because sweating, friction and increased blood pressure can affect the treated area. Your clinical team will advise when you can gradually resume exercise.

What happens after my procedure?

You will receive aftercare instructions covering scalp care, washing, medication if prescribed and activities to avoid. Follow-up allows the clinic to monitor healing and hair growth as your result develops.

Consultation, Pricing & Privacy

Plan your consultation with answers about costs, initial assessments and photo privacy.

How much does hair-loss treatment cost?

Cost depends on the diagnosis and treatment required. Non-surgical treatments and hair transplantation have different pricing structures, and transplant pricing may also depend on the complexity and extent of the procedure.

Can I get an estimate before visiting the clinic?

You can start by sharing clear photos of your hairline, top, crown and donor area for an initial assessment. This can help the team understand your concern before recommending the next step. A final treatment plan may still require an in-person examination.

What happens during a hair consultation?

The consultation focuses on your hair-loss pattern, scalp condition, history, expectations and possible treatment options. The goal is to understand your case first before recommending a treatment pathway.

Are the photos I submit kept private?

Photos submitted for assessment should be handled as personal medical information and used for consultation and treatment planning. If privacy is important to you, you can also ask the clinic how your photographs are stored and who has access to them.
